{{short description|American physicist}}
'''Hugh Elliot Montgomery''' (born March 21, 1948<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.jlab.org/div_dept/news/releases/2008/MontCV.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae Hugh Elliot Montgomery |date=2008-03-15 |accessdate=2018-10-29}}</ref>) is a British-born US [[physicist]]. He had been appointed director of the [[Jefferson Lab|Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility]] in 2008. From 2002 until 2008, he was associate director for research at the [[Fermilab|Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] in [[Batavia, Illinois]].<ref>{{cite web |work= Jefferson Lab News Release |url= https://www.jlab.org/news/releases/hugh-montgomery-named-jlabs-new-director |title= Hugh Montgomery Named JLab's New Director |date= 2008-04-03 |accessdate= 2018-10-29}}</ref>

Montgomery received his Ph.D. in physics from the University of Manchester in 1972. He worked at the Daresbury Nuclear Physics Laboratory and Rutherford High Energy Laboratory until 1978. From 1978 to 1983, he was a staff member at [[CERN]]. He was Spokesperson of the [[D0 experiment|D0]] Experiment at Fermilab from 1993 to 1999.

Montgomery was awarded the very prestigious 2016 [[Glazebrook Medal]] by the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Glazebrook Medal and prize of the Institute of Physics |url= http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/glazebrook/medallists/page_67611.html |accessdate= 1 July 2016}}</ref>
